A big thank you to Datalab for building Indra OCR and letting Scanly run it right on your phone. It\'s why Scanly can read 100+ languages.
Latin script only. Pages in other scripts, such as Hindi, Tamil, Arabic or Chinese, come out empty or garbled. Switch to Indra OCR for those.
5 script families, read in one pass. Each line is routed to the right recognizer, so pages that mix languages work too.
Reads 100+ languages across many scripts, including Hindi, Tamil, Arabic, Chinese and Japanese. Slower than ML Kit.
Google\'s fast on-device recognizer. Best for Latin-script languages like English, Spanish and French.
If a page\'s text looks empty or garbled, it is probably in a script ML Kit can\'t read. Switch to Indra OCR, then use Re-read existing pages.
Switching engines only affects new reads. Pages you already have can be re-read from this screen, and text you corrected yourself is never replaced.
If Indra OCR can\'t read a page, takes too long or stops, ML Kit reads it instead.
ML Kit is the safety net
Both engines run on the device. Pages are never uploaded to read them.

ML Kit is the default. It is fast and very accurate for Latin-script languages such as English, Spanish, French and German.\n\nIndra OCR is for everything else. It reads 100+ languages, including Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, Arabic, Urdu, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Thai, and handles pages that mix languages. It is experimental and slower, so pages take longer to become searchable.
After you scan, Scanly reads the words on each page. That text is what lets you search your library by what a page says, copy or share text from a scan, and export it.
